title: The Man Whose Left Side Gave Way After Lunch — A Stroke on Top of New Diabetes and Hypertension

sections.heading: The Patient's Story
sections.content:
He is 60 years old, presenting with weakness in both his left arm and leg for the past three days. He had been apparently well one and a half years ago, when he had 3–4 episodes of vomiting along with giddiness and weakness, at which point he was diagnosed with hypertension. About six months later he developed a wound that healed slowly, leading to a diagnosis of type 2 diabetes.

Five days before this presentation, he suddenly developed left-sided weakness after eating lunch, along with his mouth deviating to the right and slurred speech. He has known hypertension for a year and a half, on atenolol, and known diabetes for a year, on metformin. He occasionally drinks toddy and smokes one chutta a day.

sections.heading: What the Work-Up Showed So Far
sections.content:
- **General exam:** afebrile; pulse 55 bpm; respiratory rate 14/min; blood pressure 140/90 mmHg; oxygen saturation 99%; random blood glucose 171 mg/dL; no pallor, icterus, cyanosis, clubbing, or koilonychia
- **Systemic exam:** heart sounds normal; bilateral air entry present; abdomen soft and non-tender with normal bowel sounds
- **Neurological exam:** higher mental functions normal; speech slurred; no signs of meningeal irritation; decreased (hypotonic) tone in the left upper and lower limbs with normal tone on the right; power 5/5 on the right upper and lower limbs versus 0/5 in the left upper limb and 4/5 in the left lower limb; reflexes brisker on the left (biceps, triceps 3+) compared to the right (2+), with an extensor plantar response on the left and flexor on the right

**Working diagnosis:** Given his acute left-sided weakness with facial and speech involvement on a background of recently diagnosed hypertension and diabetes, the presentation was consistent with an acute cerebrovascular accident (stroke).

sections.heading: How the Story Unfolded on the Ward
sections.content: He was started on aspirin-atorvastatin combination therapy, continued telmisartan for blood pressure control, IV thiamine and B-complex supplementation, and continued metformin for his diabetes, with blood pressure, temperature, pulse, and glucose monitored every four hours.
